260:
(a) Employees are covered under the Worker's Compensation Act of Georgia. If an employee is injured on the job, such must be reported to the supervisor immediately. Per law, failure to report timely could jeopardize your claim. The supervisor must report the injury to human resources on the day of the occurrence. A supervisor accident/incident investigation report must be turned in to human resources as soon as possible. The employee shall be drug tested, as the city is a drug-free workplace.
(b) The city will seek return to work opportunities through the use of transitional employment for employees who are temporarily disabled due to an on-the-job injury as quickly as medically possible. Transitional employment opportunities will be considered in all departments, not just the department in which the injured employee was working before the injury or illness occurred.
(c) If an employee injured on the job is unable to perform any work and this is substantiated by a doctor's report, the employee may draw worker's comp, up to the limit stipulated by law, starting on the eighth day of disability. The city will pay the full salary for any loss time during the first 40 hours of a worker's comp disability, then worker's comp benefits will begin on the eighth day of disability. An employee may use any accumulated leave to cover the time between the first 40 hours and the eighth day of disability. An employee may also opt to receive only the worker's comp authorized by law, which most often will be monetarily less than an individual's normal salary. In any case, no employee may be drawing full pay (provided by the city of accumulated leave) and worker's comp at the same time.
(Ord. of 3-6-2020, ch. 10(I))
261:
Every employee should have the opportunity to vote. Any employee whose service schedule does not provide four consecutive hours to vote while polls are open will be granted up to two paid hours off to vote. We select the hours employees are excused to vote. Exempt employees may be provided additional time off with pay to comply with wage and hour laws. Notify the clerk of voting leave two to ten days before the election. Present voter's receipt to clerk.
(Ord. of 3-6-2020, ch. 10(J))
262:
During an emergency following a declaration of emergency under law, upon receipt of written documentation from the head of a fire department or volunteer ambulance service documenting your status as a volunteer firefighter or member of a volunteer ambulance service, the city will grant "volunteer emergency responder" paid leave while engaged in actual performance of duties as a volunteer firefighter or an enrolled member of a volunteer ambulance service, unless the city determines absence would impose an undue hardship on the city. Provide a notarized statement from the head of the department/service certifying time you responded to emergency.
(Ord. of 3-6-2020, ch. 10(K))
263:
Full-time employees who have completed 12 months of employment are eligible for one paid day for the death of a spouse, domestic partner, parent, sibling, child, grandchild, grandparent, parent-in-law; and immediate family member of spouse. Exempt employees may be provided paid time off to comply with wage and hour laws. Requests should be made to the clerk as soon as possible. Provide verification of family relationship and attendance at funeral.
(Ord. of 3-6-2020, ch. 10(L))
264:
The city will grant reasonable and necessary leave without pay if employees are victim of a crime, to attend or participate in legal proceedings. Give the city reasonable notice of leave. Exempt employees may be provided time off with pay to comply with wage and hour laws.
(Ord. of 3-6-2020, ch. 10(M))
267:
A department director or supervisor shall have the following alternatives for disciplinary action:
(1) Verbal reprimand. A department director or supervisor may administer a verbal reprimand to correct detrimental employee behavior or poor performance, and keep a written record of reprimands, made a part of the employee's personnel file. Such should include time, date, and brief description of problem and direction given the employee. An employee may submit a written response.
(2) Written reprimand. A department director or supervisor may submit a written reprimand to an employee that has been previously given a verbal reprimand when the verbal reprimand has not resulted in the expected improvement, or when more severe initial action is warranted. A written reprimand is accompanied with a personal counseling by the department director. Copies shall be sent to human resources. Human resources shall file a copy in the personnel file. Written reprimands must contain specific time, date, offense, place of offense, signature of the employee, and statement of expected corrective action. The employee may submit a written response and/or utilize the chain of command.
(3) Suspension. The manager may suspend an employee with or without pay for disciplinary reasons. A written statement setting forth reasons for suspension and duration shall be furnished to the employee. Such shall not exceed 30 days in any one year. Copies shall be sent to human resources and placed in the employee's personnel file.
(4) Demotion. The manager may demote an employee to a lower paying position if a position is available. The city attorney will be present for benefit of the city. A written statement of the reasons for such action shall be furnished to the employee. Copies shall be sent to human resources and placed in the employee's personnel file.
(5) Dismissal. The manager may dismiss an employee per section 2-594. The employee shall attend a private conference, and be furnished notice of dismissal in writing, stating the reasons for dismissal. Copies shall be filed with human resources and placed in the employee's personnel file.
(Ord. of 3-6-2020, ch. 11(A))
269:
Personnel files are privileged, and are only to be used for the city personnel actions. Any requests for such information will be forwarded to human resources. Employees are permitted to review their own files.
(Ord. of 3-6-2020, ch. 11(C))
273:
At time of separation and prior to final payment, all records, assets, and other city property shall be transferred to the employee's department director or supervisor. Department directors or supervisor and the separated employee will sign a certification to this effect. Any amount due because of shortage in the above shall be withheld from the employee's final compensation. In the case of a department director or supervisor being terminated, the accounting shall be to the manager. All accountings must be forwarded to human resources.
(Ord. of 3-6-2020, ch. 12(B))
274:
(a) To resign in good standing, an employee shall give notice in writing to the department director or supervisor at least ten working days prior to effective date of the resignation. The director or supervisor will forward all resignations to human resources within 24 hours. Any full or part-time employee leaving in good standing will be compensated for any unused personal leave accrued.
(b) All city property, including this handbook, must be returned at the end of employment. Otherwise, the city may take action to recoup any replacement costs and/or seek the return of city property through legal recourse. Notify us if your address changes during the year discharge occurs, so your tax info will be sent to the proper address. Our city does not provide a "letter of reference."
(c) An employee who resigns in good standing shall be eligible for rehire. Such eligibility shall not be a right and is subject to the working probationary period.
(Ord. of 3-6-2020, ch. 12(C))
275:
Failure to report without valid reason and without authorized leave for two consecutive work days shall be cause for separating an employee from the payroll and reporting the employee as having abandoned their position.
(Ord. of 3-6-2020, ch. 12(D))
276:
An involuntary separation not involving delinquency, misconduct or inefficiency shall be a lay-off or furlough. To reduce workforce, employees shall be laid off on the basis of time of service, criticalness of skill and performance. Options of keeping employees elsewhere in the city may be considered. Upon separation, you may be entitled to unemployment insurance benefits. Information about unemployment insurance can be obtained from the clerk.
(Ord. of 3-6-2020, ch. 12(E))
277:
In disability other than as a result of an on-the-job injury, the department director or supervisor, or human resources may direct any employee to be examined by a physician designated by human resources. When a disability is discovered which impairs ability to perform essential functions of a job, or impairs effectiveness of others, the following action may be taken:
(1) If the disability can be corrected, the employee may be allowed a specified reasonable length of time as determined by the department director or supervisor to have it corrected. If the employee fails to take steps to have it corrected within the specified time, the employee may be subject to disciplinary action or termination.
(2) If, in the opinion of the examining physician, the disability cannot be corrected, the department director or supervisor shall attempt to reasonably accommodate the employee or place the employee in another position where the essential functions of the job can be performed satisfactorily. If that cannot be accomplished without undue hardship, the director or supervisor may take steps to separate the employee from the city service through dismissal without prejudice.
(Ord. of 3-6-2020, ch. 12(F))
278:
(a) You will be informed by clerk of licensing, certification or testing requirements. Failure to qualify or maintain such may be cause for discharge.
(b) Employees for whom operation of a vehicle is an essential duty must present and maintain a valid driver's license and clean driving record to our insurer. Changes must be reported to the clerk immediately. Violation may result in immediate termination.
(c) Any employee unable to do a job because of loss of any drivers or any other necessary license, or who fails to obtain certification required, or who fails to meet other job requirements, shall be terminated.
(Ord. of 3-6-2020, ch. 12(G))
279:
When an employee dies, all compensation due shall be paid to the estate or properly designated individual.
(Ord. of 3-6-2020, ch. 12(H))
280:
An employee may voluntarily retire at 65 years of age, which shall be considered voluntary separation, if the employee meets the requirements governing any allocable pension or defined benefit contribution plan covering the employee. The employee's right to benefits shall be determined under the plan documents.
(Ord. of 3-6-2020, ch. 12(I); Amd. No. 2025.11.001, 11-19-2025)
281:
A dismissal is a separation for definable cause, such as inefficiency, insubordination, other rule violation, or inability to perform the required work satisfactorily.
(Ord. of 3-6-2020, ch. 12(J))
284:
The city makes available the following, subject to availability of an insurer and policies, adopted by the city upon recommendation of human resources. More detail can be obtained from human resources.
(1) Group health insurance.
(2) Retirement plan.
(3) Short-term disability.
(4) Defined benefit contribution plan. Upon beginning employment, employees may participate in the city's defined contribution plan (403b, 457b, or simple IRA). After completing one year of employment, the city may match up to three percent of the gross wages each pay period for an employee who participates in the city's defined contribution plan (403b, 457b, or simple IRA).
(Ord. of 3-6-2020, ch. 13; Amd. No. 2025.11.001, 11-19-2025)
287:
The policies and procedures in the manual are not an implied or written contract. The employment relationship is at-will and may be terminated with or without cause and with or without notice, any time, at the discretion of the city. Only council has the authority to alter the at-will nature of this relationship. This manual is for information purposes only. It does not contain all information you will need during your employment. You will receive additional information through various notices as well as orally through your supervisor, department director, personnel committee and human resources. The city is committed to reviewing its policies, procedures and benefits periodically. Accordingly, the policies, procedures and benefits outlined in this manual are subject to review and change by the city at any time.

These policies may be amended by the city per its ordinance adoption procedure provided a notice of the proposed changes to these policies shall be posted at a conspicuous place in the city at least 14 days prior to effective date of the amendment.

State Law reference— Alcoholic beverages, O.C.G.A. § 3-1-1 et seq.
295:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Alcohol means ethyl alcohol, hydrated oxide of ethyl, or spirits of wine, from whatever source or by whatever process produced, includes all alcohol, distilled spirits, beer, malt beverage, wine or fortified wine.
Alcoholic beverage means all alcohol, distilled spirits, beer, malt beverage, wine or fortified wine.
Church means a building primarily used for public religious worship on a regular basis.
City means the city council, or alternatively, where the context demands, the area of Watkinsville.
Distilled spirits means alcohol obtained by distillation or more than 24 percent alcohol, including but not limited to all fortified wines.
Fortified wine means any alcohol more than 24 percent alcohol made from fruits, berries or grapes, by natural fermentation or by natural fermentation with brandy added. The term includes but is not limited to brandy.
Governing authority orcity means the mayor and city council; provided, however, where the context demands such, the term "city" means the geographical area within incorporated Watkinsville.
License, in article II of this chapter, means authorization to sell alcohol by the package not for consumption on premises. The term "license" in article III of this chapter means authorization to engage in sale of alcohol for consumption on premises.
Licensee, in article II of this chapter, means any person selling at retail any alcohol in unbroken packages not for consumption on premises. The term "licensee" in article III of this chapter means a person engaged in selling at retail alcohol for consumption on premises.
Lounge means a separate room where alcoholic beverages are served by the drink connected with or adjacent to a restaurant. No lounges shall be permitted.
Malt beverage means any alcohol obtained by fermentation of barley, malt, hops or any other similar product, or any combination of such products in water, containing not more than 14 percent alcohol by volume, and including ale, porter, brown, stout, lager beer, small beer and strong beer. The term "malt beverage" does not include sake, known as Japanese rice wine.
Package means a bottle, can, keg, barrel or other original consumer container.
Permit means authorization for a wholesaler or distributor for wholesale sales of alcohol to retail licensees.
Place of business means the premises described in a license issued pursuant to this chapter.
Premises means the location where a licensee is authorized to sell alcoholic beverages. The premises of restaurants shall include outdoor seating areas owned or leased by the licensee.
Private club means an entity organized and operated for pleasure, recreation and other nonprofit purposes including an organization which has received approval from the U.S. Internal Revenue Service as a 501(c)(3) organization. No private club shall be entitled to possess, serve or sell alcoholic beverages.
Restaurant means any place held out to the public where meals are actually and regularly served, without sleeping accommodations. Such place shall be air-conditioned and contain adequate and sanitary kitchen and dining equipment and seating capacity for at least 50 people, and have sufficient employees to cook and serve food for its patrons. At least one meal per day shall be served at least five days a week, except holidays, vacations and periods of redecorating. Serving of such meals shall be the principal business, with the serving of alcohol consumed on the premises as only incidental to such business. A restaurant shall derive at least 65 percent of its total annual gross food and beverages sales from the sale of prepared meals or prepared food and shall have food sales in excess of $150,000.00 per calendar year (January 1 through December 31).
School means a building, publicly or privately owned, used for teaching and includes below the first grade usually serving pupils of the four to six year age group and fostering such pupils' natural growth and social development through constructive play, including pre-K and kindergarten.
Wholesaler or wholesale distributor means any person who sells alcoholic beverages to other wholesale dealers, to retail dealers, or to retail consumption dealers. Wholesale distribution centers of operation are not allowed within the city limits. Wholesalers are permitted to deliver to licensees within the city limits; wholesalers are not permitted to operate a center of operation for a wholesaling business in the city limits.
Wine means any alcohol containing not more than 24 percent alcohol by volume made from fruits, berries or grapes, either by natural fermentation or by natural fermentation with brandy added. The term "wine" includes, but is not limited to, all sparkling wines, champagnes, combinations of such beverages, vermouths, special natural wines, rectified wines, and like products. The term "wine" does not include cooking wine mixed with salt or other ingredients to render it unfit for human consumption as a beverage. A liquid shall first be deemed to be a wine at that point when it conforms to the definition of wine contained in this section.
(Ord. of 7-17-2019(1), § 1)
296:
A licensee under this chapter shall post in a conspicuous place in such person's establishment a sign in letters at least four inches high reading: "Sale of alcoholic beverages to persons under 21 years of age strictly prohibited." The licensee shall also post in a conspicuous place in the licensed premises a sign in letters at least four inches high reading: "Warning: Drinking alcoholic beverages during pregnancy can cause birth defects."
(Ord. of 7-17-2019(1), § 2)
299:
Alcohol under this article will be for consumption only off the premises of the licensee.
(Ord. of 7-17-2019(1), § 32)
300:
(a) No license shall be granted unless such person is at least 25 years of age and has been a resident of the state for a minimum of one year prior to filing an application. If a corporation or LLC should be an applicant, it shall designate a person responsible for all matters regarding the business, and that person shall be at least 25 years of age.
(b) No official or employee or member of the city shall be eligible for a license; however, any nonprofit corporation whose earnings are purely civic and for community purposes may be organized or owned by or operated by members of the city, and/or by officials or employees of the city as the case may be.
(c) Per O.C.G.A. § 3-3-21, no license shall be granted to any person unless the entire business premises of the proposed location is situated beyond 100 yards of any housing authority property and beyond 100 yards from the property line of any school ground or college campus and not less than 100 yards from any building used as an alcohol rehabilitation center, and, furthermore, the front door of the retail sales establishment is beyond 150 feet from the front door of any church. The distance shall be measured by most direct route of travel on the ground. Each application shall include a scale drawing of the location of the proposed premises showing distance to nearest housing authority property, school and alcohol rehabilitation center or a certificate of a registered surveyor that such location complies with this section.
(d) A separate license shall be required for each place of business.
(e) No license shall be issued unless the building is complete and detailed plans of the building and outside premises are attached to the application, unless proposed plans and specifications and a building permit of a proposed building comply with all ordinances of the city, all regulations of the state revenue commissioner, and all the laws of the state. The proposed building shall also be subject to final inspection and approval when completed by the building inspector. Each building in which the business will be located shall contain sufficient lighting so the building and the premises on all sides shall be readily visible at all times from the street. The lighting shall illuminate the inside retail area and all the outside premises. Each applicant shall attach evidence of ownership or a copy of the lease if the applicant is leasing.
(f) The licensee shall not have been convicted of or pled nolo contendere to a felony or a misdemeanor involving moral turpitude within ten years of the date of application. As to entity applicants, including, without limitation, LLCs, corporations, and partnerships, the foregoing requirements, regarding no such convictions, apply to any owners who own a 20 percent or more interest in the entity. All such owners, shall furnish picture ID and provide a copy of their state alcohol license.. The managers shall also submit to the city a complete set of fingerprints for state and federal law enforcement background check and be photographed by the city.
(g) Licensee shall be responsible for the management and operation of the business.
(h) The applicant shall make a sworn statement of such person's qualifications according to this section and shall place the statement on file with the city clerk before any license is issued.
(i) If the application covers a partnership, all members of the partnership must be qualified to obtain a license and must make sworn statements of these qualifications.
(j) If the application covers a corporation or LLC, the manager of the proposed licensed premises must be qualified to obtain a license and must make sworn statements of these qualifications. A corporate license applicant shall appoint and designate to the city an agent authorized to receive service of process under state law. If no such designation is made, the city may serve or notify the applicant or license holder at any address of the applicant or license holder known to the city.
(k) The city, in its reasonable discretion, may objectively consider any and all relevant circumstances regarding location history and proximity to residential which may reflect favorably or unfavorably on the applicant, the application or the proposed location of the business. If in its reasonable judgment circumstances are such that the granting, suspension or revocation of the license would or would not be in the best interest of the general public, such circumstances may be grounds for the decision of the city.
(l) Any misstatement or concealment shall be grounds for revocation and make the applicant liable to prosecution for perjury.
(m) When the city shall deny an application, the applicant shall have ten days following the date of notice of the denial to request a hearing before the city. The applicant shall be entitled at such a hearing to present evidence and cross-examine opposing witnesses.
(Ord. of 7-17-2019(1), § 33)
301:
Application shall be made on forms furnished by the city as follows:
(1) All applications shall be presented in person.
(2) Each applicant shall attach a completed application for a state license. Upon applicant's receipt of the state license, it shall be promptly forwarded to the city.
(3) Per O.C.G.A. § 3-3-2(c) applicant shall furnish a complete set of fingerprints for search of the files of the GCIC and NCIC for any instance of criminal activity during the last ten years.
(4) Before any license is granted, the applicant must post with the city a performance bond with an insurance company as surety. This bond shall require the faithful observance and performance by the licensee of the rules and regulations in this article. Upon the violation of this article the amount of bond to be forfeited will be determined by the seriousness of the violations as determined by the city. The bond is to be approved by the city and shall be properly executed. The bond shall be in the amount established by resolution. In lieu of the bond required hereinabove, the city may accept a letter of credit or a certificate of deposit from a FDIC insured bank in the same amount.
(5) A license shall be valid only for the calendar year on the license, and not renewed. A licensee who desires to continue in business must make a new application for next year by 12:00 noon on the first Wednesday in December of the present year. The prior year's application may be used, with complete supplementation addressing any and all changed circumstances. The accuracy of the original application and any supplemental information shall be certified under oath.
(6) Proof of compliance with all city zoning and subdivision regulations and other applicable local, state, and federal requirements.
(Ord. of 7-17-2019(1), § 34; Ord. of 3-23-2022)
302:
(a) The annual fee for a new license shall be in the amount established by resolution and shall be paid prior to the issuance of any license and shall be cash or a bank certified check. All licenses shall expire on December 31 of the year for which they were granted. No license fee shall be prorated.
(b) Every person working on a licensee's premises who may ever provide beer or wine to a customer shall be no less than 18 years of age.
(c) Each new licensee shall complete an alcohol training class, approved by the city after careful investigation of the proposed program and test by the city, prior to license approval. Every person working on a licensee's premises who may ever provide alcohol to a customer shall complete an alcohol training class, approved by the city after careful investigation of the proposed program and test by the city, prior to license approval, and within six months of a new employee's hiring date and renew such every three years. The licensee shall supply proof of such at the time of permit application. Failure to timely present such proof shall be cause for a determination by the city council of noncompliance and suspension of alcohol sales until the next meeting of the city council after proof of compliance.
(Ord. of 7-17-2019(1), § 35)
303:
No licensee, nor any agent or employee of the licensee, nor any other person shall do any of the following upon the licensed premises:
(1) Sell or deliver any alcohol to any person except in the licensee's place of business.
(2) Furnish, sell or offer for sale any alcohol on Christmas Day.
(3) Sell or possess for sale alcohol where such person does not have a license to sell or possess for sale.
(4) Receive alcohol at the premises other than by a wholesale dealer with a permit granted by the city.
(5) Knowingly and intentionally offer for sale, sell, barter, exchange, give, provide or furnish alcohol to any person confined in any jail, penal institution, correctional facility, prison camp, penitentiary or other lawful place of confinement, or to any person who is a patient or inmate of the Central State Hospital, or to any person who is noticeably intoxicated, or who is of unsound mind, or is a habitual drunkard whose intemperate habits are known to the licensee.
(6) Fail to post in a conspicuous place in the licensed premises the signs required by section 4-2.
(7) Fail to maintain on the licensed premises at all times a telephone in good working order.
(8) Knowingly allow a person with a criminal record for violence or disorder to frequent/loiter on premises.
(9) Knowingly allow any person to frequent the licensee's premises for the purpose of soliciting prostitution.
(10) Fail to report to police at the earliest possible time any known incident of a criminal nature. It shall be unlawful for a licensee to willfully withhold from police any information pertaining to any crime on premises.
(11) Knowingly allow any criminal act to be committed on the premises.
(12) Give away any ticket, token or any other item that can be exchanged for any alcoholic beverage or wine upon the purchase of any other alcoholic beverage or wine.
(13) Allow the sale of two or more alcoholic beverages or wine for a single price, or the sale of one container of alcoholic beverages or wine with a ticket, token or any other items redeemable for a subsequent container of alcoholic beverage or wine.

(Ord. of 7-17-2019(1), § 36)

305:
Licenses shall be displayed prominently at all times on the premises.
(Ord. of 7-17-2019(1), § 38)

Any wholesale distributor licensed by the state or the agent of such may be granted a permit from the city to distribute in the city upon making application for such permit to the city clerk and upon the presentation of evidence satisfactory to the city that the applicant understands and will comply fully with all terms and conditions and provisions of this article, and upon payment of an annual fee in the amount established by resolution.
(Ord. of 7-17-2019(1), § 39)
307:

310:
The business shall be open to inspection at all times by officers/officials authorized to conduct such.
(Ord. of 7-17-2019(1), § 43)
311:
There shall be no gambling, betting, games of chance, punchboards, slot machines, lotteries, tickets or chances therein or any schemes for hazarding money or any other thing of value, or in any adjoining room owned, leased or controlled by the licensee; however, the sale of state lottery tickets in compliance with the Georgia Lottery for Education Act (O.C.G.A. § 50-27-1 et seq.) is permitted.
(Ord. of 7-17-2019(1), § 44)

(Ord. of 7-17-2019(1), § 45)

The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Animal means any and all types of animals both domesticated and wild, male and female, singular and plural.
Animal control officer means an individual selected by the local governing authority pursuant to the provisions of O.C.G.A. § 4-8-22 to aid in the administration and enforcement of the provisions of this chapter.
Animal establishment means any pet shop, grooming shop, animal auction, kennel, performing animal exhibition, or animal shelter, except the term "animal establishment" shall not include veterinary medical facilities, licensed research facilities, facilities operated by government agencies, or licensed animal dealers regulated by the USDA under the provisions of P.L. 89-544 and 91-579.
Animal shelter means a facility designated or recognized by the governing authority for the purpose of impounding or caring for animals.
At large means off the premises of the owner or custodian of the animal or fowl, and not under the immediate control of the owner or custodian.
Board means the animal control board.
Dog control officer. See Animal control officer.
Fowl means any and all fowl, domesticated and wild, male and female, singular and plural.
Governing authority means the county board of commissioners and/or the city council, as the context requires or permits.
Humane manner means care of an animal to include, but not limited to, adequate heat, ventilation and sanitary shelter, wholesome food and water, consistent with the normal requirements and feeding habits of the animal's size, species, and breed.
Kennel means an establishment kept for the purpose of breeding, selling, or boarding dogs or cats or engaging in training of dogs or cats.
Licensing authority means the city or county agency or designated representative thereof charged with administering the issuance and/or revocation of permits and licenses under the provisions of this chapter.
Neutered means rendered permanently incapable of reproduction.

(1) Damages, soils, or defecates on private property other than the owner's or on public walks and recreation areas unless such waste is immediately removed and properly disposed of by the owner;
(2) Causes a disturbance by excessive barking or other noisemaking;
(3) Chases vehicles or molests, attacks, or interferes with persons or other domestic animals on public or private property.
Owner means any natural person or any legal entity, including, but not limited to, a corporation, a partnership, firm, or trust owning, possessing, harboring, keeping, or having custody or control of a dangerous dog or potentially dangerous dog within this city, or who knowingly permits a dog or other animal to be harbored or kept, or has a dog or other animal in such person's care, or who permits a dog to remain on or about the premises.

(a) The city shall enforce the latest editions of the following Georgia State Minimum Standard Codes, as adopted and amended by the state department of community affairs (DCA): the International Building Code, International Fuel Gas Code, International Mechanical Code, International Plumbing Code, National Electrical Code, International Fire Code, International Energy Conservation Code, International Residential Code, and the International Swimming Pool and Spa Code.

(c) A fire hazard includes an activity, circumstance, condition, situation, materials, material process, use or improper use of heat sources, that can cause a fire, a fire out of control, an explosion, or a related condition, such as panic from fear of smoke, fire, or explosion, that is a risk to persons, property, or health, safety and/or welfare. For the purpose of life safety as it pertains to land uses and fire inspections, and specifically for prevention of loss of life and property from fire, panic or related hazards, the city adopts and incorporates by reference the state codes, Administrative Code 120-3-3, "Rules and Regulations for State Minimum Fire Safety Standards" per O.C.G.A. § 25-2-4 to ensure all codes adopted by reference in 120-3-3 by the state are automatically included. The city's intent is that this amendment shall not be less restrictive or protective than the "state minimum fire safety standards" promulgated in conformance with O.C.G.A. § 25-2-4 and other provisions of O.C.G.A. § 25-2-1 et seq.
It is the intent of the city to incorporate by reference all provisions of the 2018 National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) Life Safety Code as adopted and modified by the state, and that whenever NFPA and/or the state change the Life Safety Code (such as the state soon adopting the recently promulgated 2024 Life Safety Code), it shall automatically be updated herein.
The city further expressly gives the county fire marshal and both city and county building inspectors the authority to perform fire safety inspections and related activities for buildings and structures not covered by O.C.G.A. § 25-2-13, and further gives them authority to enforce the latest state adopted editions of the International Fire Code (IFC) and the latest state adopted codes, standards, recommended practices, guides and methods of the National Fire Codes (NFC) by the National Fire Protection Association (NFPA), as modified by state law.

(a) The fire limits of the city for purposes of the building code shall be the city limits.
(b) Construction types; definitions.
(1) Type I-A—Fire-resistive non-combustible (commonly found in high-rise buildings and Group I occupancies).
a. Three-hour exterior walls.
b. Three-hour structural frame.
c. Two-hour floor/ceiling assembly.
d. 1½-hour roof protection.
(2) Type I-B—Fire-resistive non-combustible (commonly found in mid-rise office and Group R buildings).
a. Two-hour exterior walls.
b. Two-hour structural frame.
c. Two-hour ceiling/floor separation.
d. One-hour ceiling/roof assembly.
(3) Type II-A—Protected non-combustible (commonly found in newer school buildings).
a. One-hour exterior walls.
b. One-hour structural frame.
c. One-hour floor/ceiling/roof protection.
(4) Type II-B—Unprotected non-combustible (most common type of non-combustible construction used in commercial buildings). Building constructed of non-combustible materials, but these materials have no fire resistance.
(5) Type III-A—Protected combustible (also known as "ordinary" construction with brick or block walls and a wooden roof or floor assembly which is one-hour fire protected).
a. Two-hour exterior walls.
b. One-hour structural frame.
c. One-hour floor/ceiling/roof protection.
(6) Type III-B—Unprotected combustible (also known as "ordinary" construction; has brick or block walls with a wooden roof or floor assembly which is not protected against fire. These buildings are frequently found in warehouse districts of older cities).
a. Two-hour exterior walls.
b. No fire resistance for structural frame, floors, ceilings, or roofs.
(7) Type IV—Heavy timber (also known as "mill" construction; to qualify all wooden members must have a minimum nominal dimension of eight inches).
a. Two-hour exterior walls.
b. One-hour structural frame or heavy timber.
c. Heavy timber floor/ceiling/roof assemblies.
(8) Type V-A—Protected wood frame (commonly used in the construction of newer apartment buildings; there is no exposed wood visible).
a. One-hour exterior walls.
b. One-hour structural frame.
c. One-hour floor/ceiling/roof.
(9) Type V-B—Unprotected wood frame (examples of Type V-N construction are single-family homes and garages. They often have exposed wood so there is no fire resistance). Note exceptions in the building code for fire resistance ratings of exterior walls and opening protection.
(Ord. of 12-18-2019(3), art. 3(2))

395:
(a) General. These codes are declared to be remedial, and shall be construed to secure the beneficial interests and purposes thereof - public safety, health, and general welfare - through structural strength, stability, sanitation, adequate light and ventilation, and safety to life and property from fire and other hazards including alteration, repair, removal, demolition, use, and occupancy of buildings, structures, or premises, and by regulating installation and maintenance of all electrical, gas, mechanical, sprinkler and plumbing systems, referred to as service systems or systems. 396:
(a) Applicability.
(1) General. Where, in any case, different sections of these codes specify different materials, methods of construction, or other requirements, the most restrictive shall govern. Where there is a conflict between a general requirement and a specific requirement, the specific shall be applicable. The Watkinsville City Code, to the extent more specific, stringent or restrictive, will prevail over any code incorporated by reference, including, without limitation, the Georgia State Minimum Standard Codes, the International Existing Building Code and the International Property Maintenance Code.
(2) Building. The International Building Code, adopted and amended by the DCA, applies to construction, alteration, repair, equipment, use and occupancy, location, maintenance, removal, and demolition, of every building or structure or any appurtenances connected or attached to such buildings or structures, except one- and two-family dwellings.
(3) Electrical. The National Electrical Code, adopted and amended by the DCA, applies to electrical systems, including alterations, repairs, replacement, equipment, appliances, fixtures, fittings, and appurtenances thereto.
(4) Gas. The International Fuel Gas Code, adopted and amended by the DCA, applies to gas piping, gas appliances, and related accessories as covered in this Code. These requirements apply to gas piping systems from point of delivery to inlet connections of appliances and installation and operation of residential and commercial gas appliances and related accessories, except one- and two-family dwellings.
(5) Mechanical. The International Mechanical Code, adopted and amended by the DCA, applies to mechanical systems, including alterations, repairs, replacement, equipment, appliances, fixtures, fittings and/or appurtenances, including ventilating, heating, cooling, air conditioning and refrigeration systems, incinerators, and other energy related systems, except one- and two-family dwellings.
(6) Plumbing. The International Plumbing Code, adopted and amended by the DCA, applies to all plumbing, including alterations, repairs, replacement, equipment, appliances, fixtures, fittings, and appurtenances, and when connected to water or sewer.
(7) One- and two-family dwellings and their accessory structures. In addition to the codes herein, the International Residential Code, adopted and amended by the DCA, applies to building, mechanical, and gas systems in new one- and two-family dwellings and their accessory buildings, plus additions, alterations, renovations and repairs of existing dwellings.
(8) Energy. The International Energy Conservation Code, adopted and amended by the DCA, regulates the design of building envelopes for adequate thermal resistance and low air leakage and the design and selection of mechanical, electrical, service water heating, and illumination systems and equipment that will enable effective use of energy in new construction.
(b) Federal and state authority. The codes shall not be held to deprive any federal or state agency, or any applicable governing authority having jurisdiction, of any power or authority it had on the effective date of the adoption of the construction codes or of any remedy then existing for the enforcement of its orders, nor shall it deprive any individual or entity of its legal rights as provided by law.
(c) Appendices. Appendices referenced are an integral part of the codes.
(d) Referenced standards. Standards referenced in the construction codes shall be considered an integral part of the codes. If specific portions of a standard are denoted by code text, only those portions of the standard shall be enforced. Where code provisions conflict with a standard, the code provisions shall be enforced.
(e) Maintenance. All buildings, structures, electrical, gas, mechanical, and plumbing systems, existing and new, and all parts thereof, shall be maintained in a safe and sanitary condition. All devices or safeguards required by the codes when constructed, altered, or repaired, shall be maintained in good working order. The owner, or designated agent, shall be responsible for maintenance of buildings and all systems.
(Ord. of 12-18-2019(3), art. 2(3))
397:
(a) General. Alterations, repairs, or rehabilitation work may be made to any existing structure, building, electrical, gas, mechanical, or plumbing system without requiring the building, structure, plumbing, electrical, mechanical, or gas system to comply with all the requirements of the codes, if the alteration, repair, or rehabilitation work conforms to the requirements of the codes for new construction. The building official shall determine the extent to which the existing system shall be made to conform to the requirements of the codes for new construction.
(b) Change of occupancy. If the occupancy classification of any existing building or structure is changed, the building, electrical, gas, mechanical, and plumbing systems shall be made to conform to the codes as required by the building official.
(c) Special historic buildings. The codes shall not be mandatory for existing buildings or structures identified and classified by the state or city as historic buildings when such are judged by the building official to be safe and in the public interest of health, safety, and welfare regarding any proposed work.
(d) Maintenance and repair. Owners shall not allow structures to deteriorate by failing to provide maintenance and repair. Decay, deterioration and structural defects, jeopardize structural integrity and pose hazards. All structures shall be kept free from the following structural defects and conditions. Owners shall maintain and repair such owners' structures as to not endanger the property with the following violations which jeopardize structural integrity:
(1) Foundations. Foundations shall support the structure as originally constructed, and be free of deterioration, holes, cracks and buckling.
(2) Structural member violations. Defective or deteriorated floor supports, or structural members of insufficient size to carry loads safely. Members of walls, partitions or other vertical supports that split, lean, list or buckle due to defective material or deterioration. Structural members of ceilings and roofs, or other horizontal structural members, which sag, split or buckle or are of insufficient size to carry imposed loads with safety. Interior staircases shall be maintained in good repair.
(3) Exterior surfaces and materials violations. Floors, walls and roofs having holes, cracks and loose, warped, protruding or rotting boards or any other condition admitting moisture or other elements. Exterior surfaces improperly exposed to the weather, which shall be repaired and weatherproofed to protect from further deterioration. Masonry joints shall be maintained. Fireplaces or chimneys which list, bulge or settle or are of insufficient size or strength to carry loads with safety. Such shall be maintained/repaired to as to be in good repair.
(4) Weather protection, ventilation. Lack of weather protection, or a fault or defect which renders it unsafe or not weathertight, are violations. Windows, exterior doors and siding shall be watertight. Flashing, including at chimneys, doors, and windows, shall be in good repair. Downspouts and gutters shall be maintained so rain runoff is directed away from the structure. Foundation and attic vents shall be maintained to ventilate the crawl and attic spaces.
(5) Stairways, porches and appurtenances. Exterior staircases, porches and appurtenances thereto shall be maintained in good repair.
(6) Rodent, termite infestation. Structures shall be free of wood boring insects and rodents.
(7) Security and utilities. Unoccupied buildings shall be secured to prevent intrusion, and utilities shall be properly disconnected.
(8) Dependencies, additional site features. Tree limbs shall be trimmed away, and tree roots cleared away from foundations. Soil erosion and deposition shall not be allowed to endanger structures.
(e) Permit; bond.
(1) It shall be unlawful for any person to relocate a building, house or similar structure without having first obtained from the city a permit therefor and having paid the required fee for the issuance of said permit.
(2) Upon the issuance of a permit, the holder thereof shall post with the city clerk either a cash bond in the amount of $1,000.00 or a letter of credit from a banking institution, authorized by the state to provide banking services, upon the following conditions:
a. The bond or letter of credit shall be returned to the holder upon satisfactory completion of the project.
b. Should the project remain unfinished, kept in an unsafe manner, or should the holder fail to clear the lot of all debris and materials within the time specified on the permit, the city manager or a designated agent shall have authority to notify the holder of the permit that the city shall complete the project in a satisfactory manner at the permit holder's expense.
c. If the expense is less than the bond posted or identified in the letter of credit, the remainder shall be returned to the permit holder.
d. If the cost is greater than the bond or letter of credit, such difference shall be due and payable to the city, and upon authorization by the city council, shall be assessed against the property.
(Ord. of 12-18-2019(3), art. 2(4); Ord. of 10-21-2020, § 1)
398:
(a) Creation of building department. There is established the building department and the person in charge (and designees) shall be known as the building official. The city shall establish the qualifications for the building official and other code enforcement personnel. The duties of the department may be contracted out in full to a third-party entity.
(b) Restrictions on employees. An officer or employee connected with the department shall not be financially interested in the furnishing of labor, material, or appliances for the construction, alteration, or maintenance of a building, structure, service, system, or in the making of plans or of specifications thereof, unless such department officer or employee is the owner of such. This officer or employee shall not engage in any other work which is inconsistent with such officer's or employee's duties or conflict with the interests of the department.
(c) Records. The building official shall keep a record of the business of the department. The records shall be open to public inspection per O.C.G.A. tit. 50, ch. 18, art. 4 (O.C.G.A. § 50-18-70 et seq.).
(d) Liability. (e) Reports. The building official shall submit a report each year covering the work of the building department during the preceding year, and may incorporate a summary of the decisions during said year.
(Ord. of 12-18-2019(3), art. 2(5))
399:
(a) General. The building official or city council's designee is authorized and directed to enforce the codes and interpret the codes consistent with their intent and purpose. The city may contract with a third party to provide the duties of the building official.
(b) Right of entry.
(1) When necessary to make an inspection, or when the building official has reasonable cause to believe there exists a condition or code violation which makes such building, structure, premises, electrical, gas, mechanical, or plumbing systems unsafe, dangerous, or hazardous, the building official may enter at all reasonable times to inspect or to perform any duty imposed on the building official by these codes, but if such is occupied, such official shall first present proper credentials and request entry. If such is unoccupied, the building official shall first make a reasonable effort to locate the owner or other persons having control and request entry. If entry is refused, the building official shall have recourse to every remedy under law to secure entry.
(2) When the building official shall have first obtained a proper inspection warrant or other remedy provided by law to secure entry, no owner or occupant or any other persons having control shall fail or neglect, after proper request is made as herein provided, to promptly permit entry therein by the building official for inspection and examination pursuant to the construction codes.
(c) Stop-work orders. Upon notice from the building official, work on any building or system contrary to the codes or in a dangerous or unsafe manner, shall immediately cease. Notice shall be in writing and given to the owner of the property, or agent, or the person doing the work, and shall state conditions under which work may be resumed. In an emergency, the building official shall not be required to give a written notice prior to stopping work.
(d) Revocation of permits.
(1) Misrepresentation of application. The building official may revoke a permit or approval, issued under the codes, if there has been a false statement or misrepresentation of material fact in the application or plans.
(2) Violation. The building official may revoke a permit upon determination that the construction, erection, alteration, repair, moving, demolition, installation or replacement of the building, structure, electrical, gas, mechanical, or plumbing systems is in violation of, or not in conformity with, the codes.
(e) Unsafe buildings or systems. All buildings or systems which are unsafe, unsanitary, or do not provide adequate egress, or which constitute a fire hazard, or are otherwise dangerous to human life, or which in relation to existing use, constitute a hazard to safety or health, are considered unsafe buildings or service systems.
(f) Requirements not covered by Code. Any requirements necessary for strength, stability, or proper operation of a building or system, or for the public safety, health, and general welfare, not covered by the codes, shall be determined by the building official.
(g) Alternates. The codes are not to prevent use of a material or method not specifically prescribed by them, if such alternate has been approved by the building official, who shall approve such alternate, if it is at least the equivalent of that prescribed in the codes, in quality, strength, effectiveness, fire resistance, durability, and safety. The building official shall require sufficient evidence to substantiate any claim regarding the alternate.
(Ord. of 12-18-2019(3), art. 2(6))
400:
(a) Permit application.
(1) Required. Anyone who desires to construct, enlarge, alter, repair, move, demolish, change occupancy of, remove, convert, or replace a building or system regulated by the codes, shall first make application to the building official and obtain the required permit, and in the case of demolition of a structure older than 50 years, from city council. A permit shall only be issued to a licensed contractor, or an owner of a residential structure being altered.
(2) Work authorized. A building or system permit gives the right to construct or install the work shown in the drawings and specifications with the application. If not on said drawings and specifications, separate permits shall be required.
(3) Minor repairs. Minor repairs less than $5,000.00, and roof replacement, siding and trim repair and gutter replacement, may be made with approval of the building official without a permit, if such repairs do not violate any codes.
(4) Information. Each application, with required fee, shall be filed with the building official on the form and contain a general description of the work. The application shall be signed by the owner, or authorized agent. It shall indicate the proposed occupancy of all parts of the building and of that portion of the site or lot not covered by the building, and contain other information required by the building official.
(5) Time. An incomplete application shall be deemed abandoned six months after the date of application. One or more extensions, not more than 90 days each, may be allowed by the building official, if requested in writing and justifiable cause is demonstrated.
(b) Drawings and specifications.
(1) Requirements. When required by the building official, two or more copies of specifications and scale drawings, with sufficient clarity and detail to indicate the work, shall accompany the application. Such shall contain information, notes or otherwise, as to quality of materials, where quality is essential to conformity with the codes. Such shall be specific, and the codes shall not be cited as a whole or in part, nor shall the term "legal" or its equivalent be used, as a substitute for specific information. All information, drawings, specifications and accompanying data shall bear the name and signature of the person responsible for the design.
(2) Additional data. The building official may require details, computations, stress diagrams, and other data necessary to describe the construction and the basis of calculations. All drawings, specifications, and data required by the building official to be prepared by an architect or engineer shall be affixed with such architect's or engineer's official seal.
(3) Design professional. The design professional shall be an architect or engineer legally registered in the state and shall affix such design professional's official seal to said drawings, specifications, and accompanying data, for all Group A, E, and I occupancies; buildings and structures three stories or more high; buildings and structures 5,000 square feet or more in area. For all other buildings and structures, the submittal shall bear the certification of the applicant that some specific state law exception permits its preparation by a person not so registered. Exception: Single-family dwellings and their accessory buildings, regardless of size, shall require neither a registered architect nor engineer, nor a certification that an architect or engineer is not required.
(4) Structural and fire resistance integrity. Plans for all buildings shall indicate how required structural and fire resistance integrity will be maintained where a penetration of a required fire resistance wall, floor, or partition will be made for conduits, pipes, and systems and indicate in sufficient detail how the fire integrity will be maintained where required fire resistance floors intersect the exterior walls.
(5) Site drawings. Drawings shall show the location of the proposed structure and every existing structure on the lot. The building official may require a boundary line survey prepared by a qualified surveyor.
(6) Hazardous occupancies. The building official may require the following:
a. Site plan. A general site plan of legible scale with location of all buildings, exterior storage facilities, permanent accessways, evacuation routes, parking lots, internal roads, chemical loading areas, equipment cleaning areas, storm and sanitary sewer accesses, emergency equipment, and adjacent property uses. The exterior storage areas shall be identified with the hazard classes and the maximum quantities per hazard class of hazardous materials stored.
b. Floor plan. A floor plan of legible scale with all hazardous materials storage facilities in the building, to indicate rooms, doorways, corridors, exits, fire rated assemblies with hourly rating, liquid-tight rooms, and evacuation routes. Each hazardous materials storage facility shall be identified with the hazard classes and quantity range per hazard class or the hazardous materials stored.
(c) Examination of documents; plan review. The building official shall examine each application and documents, drawings, specifications, computations, and additional data, and ascertain whether the construction described is in accordance with all codes, laws and ordinances.
(d) Issuing permits.
(1) Action. The building official shall act on an application without unreasonable or unnecessary delay. If the building official is satisfied the work described in an application and the documents conforms to the codes and laws and ordinances, such official shall issue a permit.
(2) Refusal to issue. If the application and the documents do not conform to the codes or other laws or ordinances, the building official shall not issue a permit, but shall return the documents to the applicant with such official's refusal to issue such permit. Such refusal shall, when requested, be in writing and contain the reason for refusal.
(3) Foundation permit. When application for permit to erect or enlarge a building is pending, the building official may issue a permit for foundation only. The holder is proceeding at such holder's own risk and without assurance that a permit for the remainder of the work will be granted or that corrections will not be required to meet the codes.
(4) Right-of-way. A permit shall not be given for construction or alteration of a building as to affect the exterior walls, bays, balconies, or other appendages or projections fronting on a street, alley, or public lane, or the placing on any lot or premises of any building or structure removed from another lot or premises, unless applicant has made application for and received approval of such; it is the duty of the building official to see that street lines are not encroached on.
(e) Contractor responsibilities. Every contractor shall comply with all state and local rules and regulations the city has adopted. If the state requires a state license, the contractor shall supply the city with such contractor's license number before receiving a permit for work.
(f) Conditions of permit.
(1) Intent. A permit is a license to proceed with work, not authority to violate any codes. Nor shall issuance of a permit prevent the building official from requiring a correction of errors in plans, construction, or violations of the codes. If work is not commenced within six months, or is suspended or abandoned for six months, the permit shall become invalid. Written extensions of time, requested in writing, not more than 90 days each, may be allowed for justifiable cause demonstrated.
(2) Affidavit. When a permit is issued in reliance on an affidavit or the work is, in the opinion of the building official, hazardous or complex, the architect/engineer who signed the affidavit or prepared the plans shall supervise such work. Such architect/engineer shall be responsible for conformity with the permit, provide contemporaneous inspection reports, and upon completion, file with the building official an affidavit that the work has been done in conformity with the plans and codes. If such architect/engineer is not available, the owner shall employ in such architect's or engineer's place a competent person/agency whose qualifications are approved by the building official.
(3) Plans. When the building official issues a permit, the building official shall notate both sets of plans "reviewed for code compliance." One set shall be retained by the building official and the other returned to the applicant. The plans shall be kept at the work site and shall be open to inspection by the building official.
(g) Fees.
(1) Prescribed fees. A permit shall not issue until the city fees have been paid. Nor shall there be an amendment to a permit until any additional fee is paid.
(2) Work before permit. Any person who commences work before obtaining the permits shall be penalized 100 percent of the permit fee in addition to the permit fees.
(3) Accounting. The building official shall keep an accurate accounting of all money collected, who paid, and the date thereof.
(4) Schedule of fees. On all work requiring a permit, a fee for each permit in the amount established by resolution shall be paid as required at the time of application.
(5) Valuations. Construction valuations shall be determined by size and type of the structure by reference to the building valuation data established from time-to-time by the International Code Council, and adjusted locally based on a square foot basis for the most recent median sales of new single-family construction built over the past two years, as reported by the county tax assessor.
(h) Inspections.
(1) Existing buildings. Before issuing a permit, the building official may examine a building or system for which application has been received, and inspect all buildings and systems, during and upon completion of work, and record such and all violations.
(2) Manufacturers and fabricators. The building official may inspect materials or assemblies at point of manufacture/fabrication, and record such and all violations.
(3) Inspection service. The building official may make the inspections required by subsection (h)(6) of this section and accept reports of recognized inspectors if such building official is satisfied as to such inspectors' qualifications. A certificate called for by the codes shall not be based on such reports unless in writing and certified by a responsible inspector.
(4) Inspections prior to certificate of occupancy (C.O.) or completion. The building official shall inspect at various intervals, and a final inspection of every building and system upon completion, prior to certificate of occupancy or completion.
(5) Posting permit. Work shall not commence until the permit is posted conspicuously on the premises, protected from the weather, to permit the building official make the required entries. This permit shall be maintained until the C.O. or completion.
(6) Required inspections. The building official shall make the following inspections, and others as necessary, and release that portion of the construction or notify the permit holder/agent of any violations to be corrected:
a. Building.
1. Foundation and foundation wall: when trenches are excavated, reinforcement is in place, and forms erected, prior to concrete.
2. Slab: prior to concrete.
3. Frame: when roof, framing, fireblocking, bracing, fasteners, concealed wiring, pipes, chimneys, ducts and vents are complete.
4. Moisture barrier: prior to the install of the exterior finishing.
5. Final: when the building is complete and ready for occupancy.
b. Electrical.
1. Underground: when trenches or ditches are excavated, conduit or cable installed, before any backfilling.
2. Rough-in: when the roof, framing, fireblocking, and bracing is in place and prior to the installation of wall or ceiling membranes.
3. Final: when the building is complete, all electrical fixtures are in place and connected, and the structure is ready for occupancy.
c. Plumbing.
1. Underground: when trenches or ditches are excavated, piping installed, before any backfilling.
2. Rough-in: when the roof, framing, fireblocking, bracing and soil, waste, and vent piping are done, before wall or ceiling membranes.
3. Final: when the building is complete, all plumbing fixtures are connected, and the structure is ready for occupancy.
4. Note: See section 312 of International Plumbing Code for required tests.
d. Mechanical.
1. Underground: when trenches/ditches are excavated, underground duct and fuel piping installed, before any backfilling.
2. Rough-in: when the roof, framing, fireblocking, bracing and all ducting, and other concealed components are complete, prior to installation of wall or ceiling membranes.
3. Final: when the building is complete, the mechanical system is connected, and the structure is ready for occupancy.
e. Gas.
1. Rough piping: when all new piping is installed, before piping is covered/concealed or fixtures or appliances connected.
2. Final piping: when all piping authorized is installed, after all portions to be concealed are concealed, before any fixtures or appliances connected. This shall include a pressure test.
3. Final: To be made on all new gas work and existing systems affected by new work or any changes, to ensure compliance with all the codes and to ensure that the gas system is per reviewed plans.
f. Energy.
1. Foundation: before slab concrete is poured, to verify perimeter insulation has been installed correctly.
2. Frame: before exterior wall insulation is concealed, to check the insulation and confirm all holes and cracks through the structure envelope have been sealed appropriately to restrict air passage.
3. Final: when the building is complete and ready for occupancy, to verify installation and R-value of ceiling and floor insulation and verify correct SEER ratings on appliances.
(7) Release. Work shall not be done on any part of a building or system beyond the point indicated in each successive inspection without a written release from the building official. Such release shall be only after an inspection of each successive step as indicated by each of the foregoing inspections.
(8) Reinforcing steel, structural frames, insulation, plumbing, mechanical, or electrical systems. No such systems or work shall be covered or concealed without first obtaining a release from the building official.
(9) Plaster fire protection. Where plaster is used for fire protection, the permit holder shall notify the building official after lathing and backing. Plaster shall not be applied until release from the building official.
(i) Certificates.
(1) Certificate of occupancy.
a. Building occupancy. A building shall not be occupied or a change made in occupancy, nature, or use of a building or part thereof until after the building official issues a C.O. It shall not issue until all systems have been inspected for compliance with the codes and other laws and ordinances and released by the building official.
b. Issuing C.O. Upon satisfactory completion of construction per the codes, plans and specifications, and after final inspection, the building official shall issue a C.O. stating nature of the occupancy permitted, number of persons for each floor, and allowable load per square foot for each floor per the codes.
c. Temporary occupancy. A temporary C.O. may issue for a portion of a commercial building, which in the opinion of the building official, may safely be occupied prior to final completion. The temporary C.O. shall be forfeited if the final C.O. is not issued within 90 days.
d. Existing building C.O. A C.O. for an existing building may be sought by making application to the building official, who may require two sets of drawings, or a general inspection, or both. If the building conforms to the codes and applicable laws and ordinances, a C.O. shall be issued.
(2) Certificate of completion. Upon satisfactory completion of a building or system, a certificate of completion may be issued, as proof that it is released for connection to a utility system. This does not grant authority to occupy a building prior to C.O.
(3) Service utilities.
a. Connection. No one shall connect from a utility to a building or system, until release by the building official and a certificate of occupancy or completion.
b. Temporary. The building official may authorize temporary connection of a building or system to a utility for testing systems under a temporary C.O.
c. Disconnect. The building official may authorize disconnection of utility service in case of emergency to eliminate a hazard. The building official shall try to notify the utility and, when possible, the owner and occupant, of the decision to disconnect prior to such. If not notified prior to disconnecting, the owner or occupant shall be notified as soon as practical thereafter.
(j) Floor loads.
(1) Occupancy. A building shall not have floors loaded beyond safe capacity. Occupancy is allowed only when the building official is satisfied capacity will not be exceeded.
(2) Storage, factory-industrial, etc., occupancies. The owner or occupant of any building where excessive floor loading may occur, shall employ a competent architect or engineer in computing safe load capacity. Such computations shall be filed, accompanied by an affidavit from the architect or engineer stating safe allowable floor load on each floor in pounds per square foot uniformly distributed.
(3) Signs. In every building or part thereof used for storage, industrial, or hazardous purposes, the safe floor loads, approved by the building official, shall be marked on plates and securely affixed by the owner conspicuously in each story. Such shall not be removed or defaced, and if removed or defaced, shall be replaced by the owner.
(Ord. of 12-18-2019(3), art. 2(7))

(a) Council. The council shall have the power to hear appeals of decisions and interpretations of the building official and consider variances.
(b) Appeals process.
(1) Decision of building official. The owner of a building or system may appeal a decision of the building official to the council whenever any one of the following conditions are claimed to exist:
a. The building official rejected or refused to approve the construction proposed or materials to be used in a building or service system.

409:
The historical heritage of the city is among its most valued and important assets, and the preservation of this heritage is essential to the promotion of the health, prosperity and general welfare of the people. Demolition by neglect of historic buildings, and unregulated new developments in historic areas, in a traditional, historic 200+ year old community such as Watkinsville, produce a devastating effect on town character and quality of life.
Watkinsville seeks to enhance the opportunities for tax benefits and the protection, preservation and rehabilitation of historic properties and historic districts. The city cherishes its citizens and its heritage. Over the last 20 years, Watkinsville has been actively transformed into a desirable and walkable location to reside, do business and visit, but has lost several historic structures over those decades due to demolition and demolition by neglect.
It is in the public interest to promulgate regulations to best protect historic property and the health, safety and welfare of the residents. Historic preservation and careful planning, particularly in historic areas and along historic corridors, can preserve historic homes and allow new development to be blended into existing historic areas without compromising the unique character of Watkinsville. To preserve the city's historic ambiance and character, standards are necessary to prevent the loss of our priceless historic treasures and protect our historic areas.
To stimulate revitalization of business districts and historic neighborhoods, to protect and enhance local historic attractions to tourists and thereby promote and stimulate business, to enhance the opportunities for tax benefits, and to provide for designation, protection, preservation and rehabilitation of historic properties and districts and to participate in programs to do the same: Mayor and council declare it to be the purpose and intent of this article to establish a uniform procedure for the protection, enhancement, perpetuation and use of districts, and buildings having a special historical, interest or value, per this article.
(Ord. of 2-21-2024, § I)

Abuse of discretion. Decision of commission based on a clearly erroneous judgment that is clearly unreasonable, erroneous, or arbitrary and not justified by the facts or this article. See Code of Ordinances for other applicable definitions
Building. A structure, permanent or temporary, to shelter any form of human activity; may refer to a historically related complex such as a courthouse and jail or a house and barn.
Certificate of appropriateness. Document evidencing approval by preservation commission of an application for a material change in appearance of a designated historic property or of a property in a designated historic district.
Exterior architectural features. Architectural style, general design and general arrangement of the exterior of a building, structure or object, including but not limited to kind or texture of the building material and the type and style of windows, doors, signs and other appurtenant architectural fixtures, features, details or elements relative to the forgoing.
Historic. A structure in a historic district generally more than 70 years old.
Historic district. Geographically definable area, which contains structures with:
(1) Special historical interest or value;
(2) One or more periods or styles of architecture typical of one or more eras in the history of the city; and

A historic district shall further mean an area designated by council as a historic district per section 8-104(b).

(a) Preliminary research.
